items.title: Flow requires challenge matching skill
items.claim: Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi's flow research (1975 onwards) identified conditions for the optimal experience. What characterises flow?

options.text: Challenge matched to skill (slightly stretching), clear goals, immediate feedback, deep concentration, sense of control, loss of self-consciousness, time distortion

items.reveal:
Csikszentmihalyi's Experience Sampling Method (ESM, 1975) gave participants pagers; when paged at random they noted what they were doing and how they felt. The pattern: deep enjoyment occurred when skill and challenge were both high.

Too little challenge → boredom; too much → anxiety. Sports psychology uses flow frameworks for performance preparation. Critics (Engeser 2012) note flow may be more available in certain activity types and that measurement post-hoc is suspect.
items.why: Flow describes a measurable state but doesn't make it easy to engineer. The conditions can be designed for; the experience can't be commanded.

items.title: Bowlby's 44 thieves
items.claim: John Bowlby's 1944 '44 Juvenile Thieves' study linked maternal separation to later antisocial behaviour. What is a key methodological criticism made of it today?

options.text: The sample was very large and well controlled
Bowlby personally interviewed the children, risking confirmation bias, and the sample was small
It was a randomised controlled trial

items.reveal:
Bowlby studied 44 juvenile thieves and 44 controls at his clinic, conducting assessments himself. Critics note the risk of bias and the difficulty of separating maternal deprivation from broader disadvantage.

Rutter (1981) drew the influential distinction between privation and deprivation.
items.why: Foundational studies often used methods we would now strengthen, but they framed questions that still drive research.

items.title: The bystander effect story
items.claim: Darley and Latane (1968) showed that people are less likely to help when others are present. The often-repeated 'Kitty Genovese 38 witnesses' story has been challenged. What did later journalism find?
items.prompt: Which is closest to the current historical record?

options.text: There were probably far fewer witnesses than reported, and some did call police
There were no witnesses at all

items.reveal:
Manning, Levine and Collins (2007) and later reporting by the New York Times showed the original 1964 article overstated the number of witnesses and inattention.

The bystander effect as a laboratory phenomenon is robust, but the case used to illustrate it was inaccurate.
items.why: Findings can be real while their iconic illustrations are not. Textbooks now distinguish the experimental effect from the journalistic story.
